codex.note: Codex has no auto-compact window or subagent model default to set; the instruction line carries the rules.

instructions.claude: - Usage: follow the `lean-usage` skill. Set an explicit `model` on every subagent by task. Coordinators (Workspace and Project) always run on Opus 5.5 at high effort. Role agents: Opus 5.5 at medium for code, small or big (high only when the task needs it), UI and visual work and VFX; Gemini 4 Carbon at medium for 3D builds; Gemini 4 Hydrogen at medium for reading many files, retrieval and searches (low for a quick lookup); no Fable 5.2 for now, Codex only when Daniel names it. Where Gemini can't run (no agy signed in, its limit, a 3D agent on a PC): 3D on Opus 5.5 medium, retrieval on Sonnet 5.5. Built-in subagents can only be Claude: retrieval on Sonnet 5.5, the rest on Opus 5.5 medium. Do small jobs inline. At most 2 subagents at once, no forks. Use contact sheets, not piles of screenshots. Time-limit every wait or background command. Put read-only steps that follow each other in one Bash call, and run only the checks for what you changed until the final full run. Compact at breakpoints, and start a fresh session with a handoff memory when the task changes.
instructions.codex: - Usage: follow the `lean-usage` skill in `~/.codex/skills/lean-usage/`. Read its Claude terms as Codex equivalents: subagents are parallel tasks or agents, Opus/Sonnet/Haiku are your strongest/standard/fastest models, and `/compact` is starting a fresh session with a handoff note. Do small jobs inline. At most 2 parallel agents. Time-limit every wait. Keep context small.
